original_question: Let s be an exponent over a finite field of odd characteristic, with s not equivalent to 1, and suppose s is nice in the sense that the differential multiplicity N(1, v) takes at most three values as v varies over the field. Must 2 always occur as one of those differential multiplicities?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1 (Introduction): the paper's 'nice exponent' conjecture.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's intended target. It correctly focuses on exponents over finite fields of odd characteristic, uses the differential-counting quantity N(1,v), captures the definition of a 'nice' exponent via the condition that these counts take at most three values, and asks exactly whether the value 2 must occur among those differential multiplicities. It also correctly excludes the degenerate class s equivalent to 1, which is part of the paper-faithful formulation of the conjectural question.
missing_details: The ambient field should be named explicitly, e.g. a finite field L of odd characteristic p.

The paper's equivalence relation on exponents should be stated explicitly: s is equivalent to t if s ≡ p^j t mod (|L|-1) for some integer j; thus 's not equivalent to 1' means s ≡ p^j mod (|L|-1) for no j.
N(1,v) should be defined from the full system N(1,v)=#{(x,y) in L^2 : x+y=1 and x^s+y^s=v}.
The quantifier should be explicit: the conclusion is that there exists v in L such that N(1,v)=2, equivalently 2 belongs to the set {N(1,v): v in L}.
The paper treats this as a conjecture/open problem, so the refined version should be phrased as a conjectural research question rather than as a theorem request.
It helps to say that 'nice' means the set {N(1,v): v in L} has cardinality at most 3, not merely that some unspecified differential multiplicity statistic has at most three values.
refined_question: Let L be a finite field of odd characteristic p, and let s be an exponent over L that is not equivalent to 1, in the sense that s ≡ p^j mod (|L|-1) for no integer j. For each v in L, define N(1,v)=#{(x,y) in L^2 : x+y=1 and x^s+y^s=v}. Suppose that the set {N(1,v) : v in L} has at most three distinct values, so that s is a nice exponent in the paper's terminology. Must there exist v in L such that N(1,v)=2?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's introductory 'nice exponent' conjecture, i.e. Conjecture 1.1, rather than at a broader neighboring problem. The nearby introductory context defines the relevant differential counts N(1,v) and the notion of a nice exponent, and Proposition 1.2 together with Theorem 1.3 are the paper's immediately adjacent results explaining why this question matters in relation to Helleseth's older three-valued-spectrum problem. So the right refinement is to keep the question exactly at the level of Conjecture 1.1, while making the field, the equivalence relation on exponents, the definition of N(1,v), and the existential meaning of '2 is a differential multiplicity' fully explicit.
